In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Fussilat

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾ We have already presented the discussion of it and of its counterparts among the verses at the beginning of Surah az-Zumar.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 3:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿A Book whose verses are made distinct﴾.

(كِتابٌ) (kitabun) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning: "This is a Book." Al-kitab (the Book) is on the pattern fi'al, in the sense of maf'ul, meaning "written" (maktub).

It is called "Book" because it is written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), as God says: ﴿Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a Preserved Tablet﴾ [al-Buruj: 21-22].

It is also written in scrolls (suhuf) with the angels, as God says: ﴿No! Indeed it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it, in honoured scrolls, exalted and purified, in the hands of scribes, noble and righteous﴾ [Abasa: 11-16].

God also says, concerning the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) of what the scrolls contain, in which the Qur'an is written: ﴿A messenger from God, reciting purified scrolls, in which are upright writings﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 2-3].

As for His words in this noble verse, ﴿whose verses are made distinct﴾: at-tafsil (distinction, detailing) is the opposite of al-ijmal (summary, generality). That is, God has made the verses of this Qur'an distinct, meaning He has clarified them and made plain in them what creatures need of the affairs of their religion and their worldly life.

The reason the agent (fa'il) is omitted in His words ﴿fussilat ayatuhu﴾ (its verses have been made distinct) is the knowledge that the detailing of the verses of this Qur'an can come from God alone.

What this noble verse includes regarding the detailing of the verses of this Book is explained in other verses, which state that God detailed it with knowledge from Himself, that the One who detailed it is All-Wise and All-Aware, that He detailed it so that He might guide people by it and show them mercy, that its detailing encompasses everything, and that there is no doubt that it is sent down from God. Such as:

• His words: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We had detailed with knowledge, a guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-A'raf: 52].

• His words: ﴿A Book whose verses are made firm, then detailed, from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware﴾ [Hud: 1].

• His words: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been fabricated other than by God, but it is a confirmation of what is before it and a detailing of the Book, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Yunus: 37].

• His words: ﴿It is not a fabricated narration, but a confirmation of what is before it and a detailing of all things, and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Hud: 111].

• His words: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed?﴾ [al-An'am: 114].

Verses of this kind are many.

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿An Arabic Qur'an for a people who know﴾ ﴿A bringer of good tidings and a warner, yet most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾.

His words: (qur'anan 'arabiyyan) (an Arabic Qur'an). We have already discussed it, and the verses that have the same meaning in the Qur'an, in surah "az-Zumar" in our commentary on His words: ﴿An Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness﴾ [az-Zumar: 28].

His words in this noble verse: ﴿for a people who know﴾ mean: its verses have been made distinct while it is (qur'anan 'arabiyyan li-qawmin ya'lamun) (an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know).

He specified them with this because they are the ones who benefit from its detailing, just as He specified them with the detailing of the verses in surah "Yunus," in His words: ﴿God did not create that except in truth; He details the verses for a people who know﴾ [Yunus: 5], and in surah "al-An'am," in His words: ﴿We have detailed the verses for a people who know﴾ ﴿And He is the One who produced you from a single soul, so there is a place of settlement and a place of storage. We have detailed the verses for a people who understand﴾ [al-An'am: 97-98], and other verses besides these.

We have clarified the reason for specifying those who benefit, with the shared matter, to the exclusion of others, in surah "Fatir," in our commentary on His words: ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish the prayer﴾ [Fatir: 18]. We showed there that the specification of them for warning, to the exclusion of others, in this verse of "Fatir," and in His words in "Ya-Sin": ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11],

• and His words in "an-Nazi'at": ﴿You are only a warner for one who fears it﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 45],

• and His words in "al-An'am": ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor﴾ (p-5) [al-An'am: 51], and the verse. This is despite the fact that the basic sense of warning is general, encompassing those mentioned and others, as His words indicate: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1].

He specified those mentioned for warning because they are the ones who benefit from it; for whoever does not benefit from warning, and whoever is not warned at all, are equal in not benefiting, as God says: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin: 10].

His words in this noble verse: ﴿a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [Fussilat: 4] are a circumstantial clause (hal) following another circumstantial clause (hal). We have already discussed it and some of its Arabic evidence at the beginning of surah "al-Kahf," in our commentary on His words: ﴿to warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers﴾ [al-Kahf: 2]. We expanded on it at the beginning of surah "al-A'raf," in our commentary on His words: ﴿A Book revealed to you, so let there be no discomfort in your breast from it, that you may warn by it, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 2].

His words in this noble verse: ﴿yet most of them turn away﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "Ya-Sin," in our commentary on His words: ﴿The word has certainly come true against most of them, so they do not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin: 7], and in surah "al-An'am," in our commentary on His words: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of God﴾ [al-An'am: 116].

His words in this noble verse: ﴿so they do not hear﴾ mean: they do not hear with the hearing of acceptance and benefit.

We have clarified this with Qur'anic verses in surah "an-Naml," in our commentary on His words: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [an-Naml: 80], and the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 5:

Allah's saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a screen."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah - Majestic and Exalted - mentions that the disbelievers declared to the Prophet ﷺ that they would not respond to him, would not believe in him, and would not accept from him what had come to them with him. They said to him: our hearts, with which we reason and understand, are "in coverings" (fi akinnah), i.e., wrappings.

Al-akinnah is the plural of kinan, which is the covering and the wrapping that covers a thing and prevents it from reaching it.

They mean that these coverings prevent them from understanding what he ﷺ invites them to. And they said: in our ears, with which we hear, there is "waqr," i.e., heaviness, which is deafness, and that this deafness prevents them from hearing anything from the Prophet ﷺ or from what he says, as Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿And those who disbelieve said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it."﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

And that between them and him there is a screen preventing them from connection and agreement, because that screen veils each of them from the other, and it stands between them and seeing what he ﷺ manifests of the truth.

Allah - Majestic and Exalted - related this statement of theirs in the context of blame, although He, the Exalted, declared that He placed coverings upon their hearts, deafness in their ears, and placed between them and His Messenger a screen when he recites the Qur'an. He, the Exalted, said in the surah "Bani Isra'il": ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden screen. And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness.﴾ [Al-Isra': 45-46]. And He, the Exalted, said in "Al-An'am": ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they should see every sign, they would not believe in it.﴾ [Al-An'am: 25]. And He, the Exalted, said in "Al-Kahf": ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 57].

This problem that we have pointed out in these verses is strong, and the aspect of its being problematic is clear: He, the Exalted, blamed them for their claim of coverings, deafness, and screen in this noble verse of "Fussilat," and in the other verses He clarified that what He blamed them for claiming is actually realized in them, and that He, the Exalted, is the One who placed it upon them.

So it is said: how are they blamed for saying something that is true in itself?

The verification of the answer to this problem is what we have mentioned repeatedly: that Allah only placed coverings upon their hearts, sealed and stamped them, placed deafness in their ears, and similar barriers to guidance - because of the fact that they hastened to disbelief and denial of the Messengers, willingly and by choice. So Allah recompensed them for that greatest sin with the obliteration of insight and blindness to guidance, as a fitting recompense.

(p-7) Thus the coverings, deafness and screen mentioned were placed upon them by Allah only as a requital for their first disbelief.

And among the recompense for an evil deed is the persistence of its doer in misguidance, and to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom in that.

The verses explicitly stating this meaning are many in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are uncircumcised." Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief.﴾ [An-Nisa': 155].

So the saying of the Jews in this verse, "our hearts are ghulf," is like the saying of the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿our hearts are in coverings﴾; because al-ghulf is the plural of aghlaf, which is one that has a wrapping on it, and al-akinnah is the plural of kinan, and the ghilaf and the kinan both have the same meaning of a concealing covering.

And Allah refuted the claim of the Jews with "bal" (rather), which is for the refuting retraction, in His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief.﴾ [An-Nisa': 155].

The "ba" in His saying "bikufrihim" (because of their disbelief) is causal, and it indicates that the cause of the sealing upon their hearts is their disbelief, and the coverings, deafness and sealing are all of one category.

And like His saying: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and they do not understand.﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 3]. The "fa" in His saying "fa-tuba'a" (so they were sealed) is causal, meaning: then they disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed because of that disbelief.

We have previously stated repeatedly that it is established in the principles of jurisprudence that the "fa" is among the particles of causation, and it is known that a legal cause is a legal reason.

Likewise the "fa" in His saying: ﴿so they do not understand﴾ is also causal, meaning: their hearts were sealed, so they, because of that sealing, (do not understand), i.e., do not comprehend anything of Allah's proofs and arguments.

This shows that sealing and coverings both ultimately have one meaning, which is the lack of understanding that arises from each of them.

For He said regarding sealing: ﴿so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand﴾.

And He said regarding coverings: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it﴾ [Al-An'am: 25], i.e., out of aversion to their understanding it, or for the sake of their not understanding it, as we have previously explained.

(p-8) And like His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [As-Saff: 5]. He clarified that their first deviation was the cause of Allah's causing their hearts to deviate, and that deviation may be by coverings, sealing, and stamping upon the hearts.

And:

• Like His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 10].

• And His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ (the verse) [Al-An'am: 110].

• And His saying: ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ [At-Tawbah: 125].

The clarification of this answer is that the disbelievers said to the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a screen,﴾ intending by that to inform him ﷺ that they do not believe in him in any way, do not follow him in any state, and do not acknowledge the truth, which is that this disbelief of theirs is the crime and sin that was the cause of the coverings, deafness and screen.

Their claim is therefore false, because Allah made for them hearts with which they understand, and ears with which they hear, contrary to what they assumed; but He caused for them the coverings, deafness and screen because of their hastening to disbelief and denial of the Messenger ﷺ.

This meaning was clarified by His refutation of the Jews in His saying about them: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are ghulf." Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief.﴾

Al-Fakhr al-Razi attempted, in his commentary on this noble verse, to answer the aforementioned problem, and said: If it is said that He related this meaning from the disbelievers in the context of blame, and also mentioned something close to it in the context of blame, saying: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are ghulf." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 88], then He, the Exalted, mentioned these three things exactly in the sense of affirmation and establishment in Surat al-An'am, saying: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [Al-An'am: 25]; then how is their combination?

We say: He did not say here that they lied in that; rather, what He blamed them for is that they said: "If we are like that, it is not permissible for us to be charged with obligations or for commands and prohibitions to be directed at us," and this second is false.

As for the first, there is nothing in the verse indicating that they lied in it. End of his quotation. And what we have mentioned is more apparent.

(p-9) The author of al-Kashshaf said in his commentary on His saying: ﴿and between us and you is a screen﴾:

If you say: is there any benefit in the addition of "min" in His saying: ﴿and between us and you is a screen﴾? I say: Yes; because if it were said: "wa-baynana wa-baynaka hijab," the meaning would be that a screen exists in the middle between the two directions.

But with the addition of "min," the meaning is that a screen has begun from us and begun from you, so the intervening distance between our direction and your direction is entirely filled with the screen, with no empty space in it. End of his quotation.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi approved this statement of his, but Ibn al-Munir critiqued az-Zamakhshari's view and clarified its invalidity, and the truth is with him in his critique of it.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and between us and you is a screen﴾, we have previously explained its interpretation and clarification by Qur'anic verses in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden screen﴾ [Al-Isra': 45].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 6:

The Exalted said: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is but one God.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands His Prophet ﷺ to say to the people: ﴿I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is but one God.﴾

The restriction (qasr) in His saying ﴿I am only a human being﴾ is relative (idafi), meaning: I do not tell you that I am an angel; rather, I am only a man from among humankind.

His saying "like you" refers to the human attributes, but Allah has favored me with what He revealed to me of His Oneness.

As the Exalted said about the Messengers in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿Their messengers said to them: We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ibrahim: 11], meaning: just as He bestowed favor upon us with revelation and messengership.

What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in this noble verse, He mentioned also at the end of Surah al-Kahf in His saying: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is but one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], and so on.

(p-10) We have already explained the aspect of the restriction of what was revealed to him ﷺ to the content of "There is no god but Allah," in His saying ﴿Say: It is only revealed to me that your God is but one God, so will you submit?﴾ in Surah Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

We have also made clear in several places in this blessed Book the denial of the polytheists that the Messengers should be human, and that they should instead be angels, and the Qur'anic verses by which Allah refuted them. We explained that in Surah Sad, in the discussion of His saying ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among them has come to them﴾ [Sad: 4], and in Surah Bani Isra'il in the discussion of His saying ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing... to His saying: ...We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 94-95].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakat, and they are, of the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾.

Some scholars of usul (legal theory) have used this noble verse as evidence that disbelievers are addressed with the branches of the Sharia (furu' al-shari'ah), because He, the Exalted, stated in this noble verse that they are polytheists and that they disbelieve in the Hereafter, and He threatened them with woe for their polytheism and their disbelief in the Hereafter, and for their not giving zakat. This holds whether we say that zakat in the verse is the well-known zakat on wealth, or the purification of the bodies through performing acts of obedience and avoiding sins.

Some of them preferred the latter view, because Surah Fussilat is among the Qur'an revealed in Makkah before the Hijrah, while the well-known zakat on wealth was prescribed after the Hijrah in the second year, as we mentioned earlier in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ [al-An'am: 141].

In any case, the verse indicates the addressing of the disbelievers with the branches of Islam, namely the carrying out of His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. What this noble verse indicates of their being addressed with that, and that they are punished for disbelief and punished for sins, has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying about them, confirming it: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ ﴿They said: We were not of those who prayed,﴾ ﴿And we did not feed the poor,﴾ ﴿And we used to engage in vain discourse with those engaged in it,﴾ ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment,﴾ ﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 42-47].

(p-11) So He, the Exalted, stated about them, confirming it, that among the causes that brought them into Saqar, that is, caused them to enter the Fire, was their not praying and not feeding the poor, and He counted that along with disbelief, due to their denial of the Day of Judgment.

A similar example is His saying: ﴿Seize him and shackle him,﴾ ﴿Then into the Blazing Fire drive him,﴾ ﴿Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits, insert him.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 30-32]. Then He explained the reason for that, saying: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah the Mighty,﴾ ﴿And did not urge the feeding of the poor.﴾ ﴿So there is not for him this Day any close friend here,﴾ ﴿Nor any food except from pus,﴾ [al-Haqqah: 33-36], and so on, along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds – for them is a reward that will never end.﴾

Al-ajr (reward) is the recompense for deeds. The recompense for the deeds of those who believe and do righteous deeds is the bliss of Paradise, and that recompense is ﴿never-ending﴾, i.e., not cut off. Al-mamnun is the passive participle of the verb manna, meaning "he cut it off." From this comes the verse of Labid ibn Rabi'ah in his Mu'allaqah:

Of a sleek, tawny (wild beast) whose prey was torn apart by vultures and wolves, whose food is not cut off (ma yumannu tacamuha).

So his words ma yumannu ta'amuha mean ma yuqta' (what is not cut off). And the saying of Dhu al-Usba':

By your life, the door of my house is not closed against a friend, nor is my goodness cut off (bi-mamnun).

What this noble verse includes, that their reward is ﴿never-ending﴾, Allah, the Exalted, has stated in other verses of His Book:

• Such as His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of Surah al-Inshiqaq: ﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that will never end.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 25].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, in Surah al-Tin: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that will never end.﴾ [al-Tin: 6].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, in Surah Hud: ﴿As for those who are made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills – a gift uninterrupted.﴾ [Hud: 108].

So His saying (ghayra majdhudh) means ghayra maqtu' (not cut off), and from this you know that ghayra majdhudh and ghayra mamnun have one meaning.

And His saying in Surah Sad: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end.﴾ [Sad: 54], i.e., it has no cessation or interruption. And His saying in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah is enduring.﴾ [al-Nahl: 96].

This which we have mentioned is what the majority (al-Jumhur) hold, unlike those who said that the meaning of ghayra mamnun is "not bestowed upon them with reproach."

Accordingly, the mann in the verse is of the same kind as the mann mentioned in His saying: ﴿Do not nullify your charities with reproach (mann) and injury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264].

As for one who said that the meaning of ghayra mamnun is "not diminished," arguing that the Arabs use mamnun to mean diminished, and they cited the saying of Zuhayr:

The superiority of the swift horses over the slow horses is such that it is not given therefor (any) mamnun or nazaq (reduced or excessive).

So his words mamnunan mean manquṣan (diminished).

And although this is valid linguistically, the more apparent view is that this is not the meaning of the verse.

Rather, its meaning is what we have already mentioned. And Allah knows best.

قال المؤلف في (دفع إيهام الإضطراب عن آيات الكتاب):

(p-٣٨٤) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat Fussilat

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Then He established Himself over the heaven.﴾

The manner of reconciling this with His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And after that He spread out the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:30] has already been explained in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then He turned to the heaven...﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:29], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 10:

Allah's saying: ﴿And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days﴾.

The apparent meaning of His saying here, "in four days," is: in the completion of four days.

The completion of the four is achieved by two days only, for He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?﴾ Then He said: "in four days," meaning: in the completion of four days.

Then He said: ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 12], so the two days are added to the previous four, and the total of the days in which He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them becomes six days.

This explanation that we have mentioned for the verse cannot be other than correct under any circumstances, because Allah, exalted is He, has stated in numerous verses of His Book that He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days,

such as His saying in "al-Furqan": ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself above the Throne, the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ [al-Furqan: 59].

And His saying, exalted is He, in "as-Sajdah": ﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or intercessor﴾ [as-Sajdah: 4].

And His saying, exalted is He, in "Qaf": ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38].

And His saying, exalted is He, in "al-A'raf": ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

And other verses besides these.

So if His saying, exalted is He, ﴿in four days﴾ were not interpreted as meaning "in the completion of four days," the meaning would be that He, exalted is He, created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in eight days; for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿in four days﴾, if interpreted as four complete days and then added to the two days in which the earth was created, mentioned in His saying: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?﴾ [Fussilat: 9], and the two days in which the heavens were created, mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 12], the total would be eight days.

No one among the Muslims has said this.

The Qur'anic texts explicitly state that it was six days, and thereby the correctness of the explanation we have mentioned is known, and the correctness of the indication of the Qur'anic verses upon it.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse, ﴿And He placed in it firm mountains from above it﴾, we have previously discussed similar verses in surah "an-Nahl" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you﴾ [an-Nahl: 15]. His saying, ﴿and blessed it﴾, means: He increased in it blessings, and blessing is goodness. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and measured therein its sustenance﴾.

Measuring (taqdir) and creating (khalq) in the language of the Arabs have one meaning.

Al-aqwat is the plural of qut, and what is meant by al-aqwat is the provisions of the people of the earth, their livelihoods, and what sustains them.

We have mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" that this verse of "Fussilat," I mean His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and measured therein its sustenance﴾, indicates the reconciliation between the verses that show the earth was created before the heaven, such as His saying here: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?﴾, then He arranged upon that with "then" (thumma) His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾, up to His saying ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾, together with some verses that show the heaven was created before the earth, such as His saying, exalted is He, in "an-Nazi'at": ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the heaven? He constructed it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And the earth after that He spread it﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 27-30].

So we said in our aforementioned book, in its text: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is the One who created for you all that is in the earth, then turned to the heaven﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29]. The verse indicates that the creation of the earth was before the creation of the heaven, by the evidence of the particle (thumma), which is for sequence and separation.

Likewise the verse of "Ha Mim as-Sajdah" also indicates that the earth was created before the heaven, for He said in it: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾, the verse.

Along with the fact that the verse of "an-Nazi'at" indicates that the spreading of the earth was after the creation of the heaven, for He said in it: ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the heaven? He constructed it﴾, then He said: ﴿And the earth after that He spread it﴾.

Know first that Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about reconciling the verse of "as-Sajdah" with the verse of "an-Nazi'at," and he answered that Allah, exalted is He, created the earth first before the heaven, not spread out, then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens in two days, then He spread the earth after that, and placed in it the mountains, the rivers, and other things.

So the origin of the creation of the earth was before the creation of the heaven, and its spreading with its mountains, its trees, and the like, after the creation of the heaven.

This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And the earth after that He spread it﴾, and He did not say "created it"; then He explained His spreading of it by His saying: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 31]. This reconciliation by which Ibn 'Abbas reconciled these two verses is clear, without difficulty, understood from the apparent meaning of the Great Qur'an, except that an objection is raised against it from this verse of "al-Baqarah."

Its clarification: Ibn 'Abbas reconciled by saying that the creation of the earth was before the creation of the heaven, and its spreading with what is in it was after the creation of the heaven.

In this verse there is an explicit statement that all that is in the earth was created before the creation of the heaven, for He said in it: ﴿He is the One who created for you all that is in the earth, then turned to the heaven﴾, the verse.

I remained for a long time pondering the solution to this objection until Allah guided me to it one day, and I understood it from the Great Qur'an.

Its clarification: this objection is removed from two aspects, each of which is indicated by a verse of the Qur'an.

(p-15) The first: that what is meant by the creation of all that is in the earth before the creation of the heaven is the linguistic creation, which is measuring (taqdir), not the creation in actuality, which is bringing out from non-existence into existence. The Arabs call measuring "creation." From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

And you indeed cut what you have created, while some of the people create but do not cut.

The evidence that the meaning of this creation is measuring is that He, exalted is He, stated this in surah "Fussilat," where He said: ﴿and measured therein its sustenance﴾, then He said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾, the verse.

The second aspect: since He created the earth unspread, and it is the origin of all that is in it, all that is in it was as if created in actuality, because its origin existed in actuality.

The evidence from the Qur'an that the existence of the origin makes it possible to apply the term "creation" to the branch, even if it does not yet exist in actuality, is His saying: ﴿And We certainly created you, then fashioned you, then said to the angels﴾, the verse [al-A'raf: 11]. So His saying "We created you, then fashioned you" means: by Our creation and Our fashioning of your father Adam, who is your origin.

Some scholars reconciled that the meaning of His saying ﴿And the earth after that He spread it﴾ is: "along with that," so the particle "after" (ba'da) means "with" (ma'a).

Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Violent, moreover, after that, ignoble﴾ [al-Qalam: 13]. On this basis, there is no difficulty in the verse.

This view is supported by the irregular reading, and Mujahid recited with it: "wal-ardha ma'a dhalika dahaha" (and the earth along with that He spread).

Others reconciled with weak opinions, because they are built upon the premise that the creation of the heaven was before the earth, which is contrary to the verified view. Among them: that "thumma" means "wa" (and). And among them: that it is for sequence in mention, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾, the verse [al-Balad: 17].

The author said in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He said to them and to the earth, "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly."﴾

What comes to mind of the incompatibility between this state and its bearers is not hidden, because the bearers are a masculine plural of rational beings, while their subject is a dual pronoun for non-rational things. Had it agreed with its subject in the dual, as comes to mind, it would have said: "We come willingly" in the feminine dual (ṭāʾiʿatayn).

The answer to this is from two angles:

The first, and the more apparent in my view, is that the plural is used for the heavens and the earth, because the heavens are seven and the earths likewise, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]. So the dual is a verbal dual, under which there are fourteen individuals.

As for the use of the plural form of rational beings, it is because the custom in the Arabic language is that when a non-rational thing is described with an attribute specific to rational beings, it is given the ruling of rational beings. Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf: 4]. Since prostration in outward appearance is among the distinctive features of rational beings, their ruling was applied to the sun, the moon and the stars because they were described with it. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ ﴿He said, "Do they hear you when you call?"﴾ ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?"﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 71–73]

(p-385) So the ruling of rational beings was applied to the idols, because the disbelievers had placed them in the rank of rational beings. From this meaning is the saying of Qays ibn al-Mulawwah:

"O flock of sandgrouse, is there anyone who will lend you his wing..."

the verse continues.

For he, when he asked the sandgrouse for lending, which is among the distinctive features of rational beings, applied to the sandgrouse the word specific to rational beings. The reason for the masculine form of the plural is that the feminine gender of the heavens and the earth is not real (ḥaqīqī).

The second angle: the meaning is: "They said, 'We come with those in us who are willing,'" so that there is in it the prevalence of the rational over the non-rational (taghlīb al-ʿāqil ʿalā ghayrihi). The first is more apparent in my view, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 12:

(p-16) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a guard﴾.

Al-masabih (the lamps): the stars.

What this verse includes regarding the adornment of the lowest heaven with the stars, we have already explained with Qur'anic verses in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who made for you the stars that you may be guided by them﴾ [al-An'am: 97].

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "and as a guard," we have already explained it with Qur'anic verses in Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We guarded them from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17], and what follows.

**Al-Shinqiti on Surah Fussilat (41:14):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels, so indeed we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾

We have already presented its clarification, with Qur'anic verses, in Surah Sad, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾ [Sad 38:4].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿So We sent against them a furious wind in ill-omened days﴾. *Al-Sarsar* (الصَّرْصَرُ): its weight in the morphological scale (*al-mizan al-sarfi*, the system of Arabic word-patterns) is *fa'fal*. Scholars of *tafsir* (Qur'anic exegesis) have two well-known views on its meaning.

The first: *al-rih al-sarsar* is the violent, strong wind that blows with a loud, terrifying sound. On this view, *al-sarsar* derives from *al-sarra*, which is the piercing cry.

From this is His saying: ﴿Then his wife came forward crying out (fi sarrah)﴾, that is, in a shriek. From the same sense comes *sarir* of the door and of the pen, that is, the sound of each.

The second: *al-sarsar* derives from *al-sirr* (الصِّرُّ), which is the severe, burning cold. From this, according to the more correct of the two interpretations, is His saying: ﴿Like a wind containing a freezing cold (sirr)﴾ [Al 'Imran: 117], that is, a wind in which there is severe, burning cold. From the same root is the saying of Hatim al-Ta'i:

*Kindle the fire, for the night is a cold night, and the wind, O kindler, is a freezing (sirr) wind,*

*Perhaps he who passes by will see your fire, and if it brings a guest, you are free.*

So his words "rih sirr" mean a wind that is cold, of severe cold.

The more apparent view is that both interpretations are correct, and that the wind mentioned combines both qualities: it is violent and fiercely blowing, and it is bitterly cold.

As for what the Exalted and Majestic One mentioned, that He destroyed 'Ad with this furious wind in those ill-omened days — that is, days that were inauspicious and calamitous, because *al-nahs* is the opposite of *al-sa'd* (good fortune) and means ill omen — this is clarified in verses of the Book of Allah.

In some of these verses He has specified the number of days and nights during which He sent the wind against them:

• As in His saying: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days in succession. So you would see the people in it lying prostrate as though they were trunks of hollow palm trees. Then do you see of them any remnant?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6–8];

• And His saying: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind. It left nothing it came upon but that it made it like ruins (ramim)﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 41–42];

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of continuous misfortune. It uprooted people as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [al-Qamar: 19–20];

• And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24–25].

This furious wind (al-rih al-sarsar) is the one meant by the thunderbolt of 'Ad in His saying: ﴿Say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad"﴾ [Fussilat: 13].

Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read the word *nahsat* (نَحْساتٍ) with a sukun on the ha' (نَحْسَاتٍ). According to this reading, *al-nahs* is either an adjective or a verbal noun functioning as an adjective.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *nahisat* (نَحِساتٍ) with a kasrah on the ha', and its basis is clear.

We have already mentioned that the meaning of *al-nahisat* is ill-omened, calamitous days.

The author of *al-Durr al-Manthur* said: al-Tastiri narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to him: "Inform me about the saying of the Mighty and Majestic One: ﴿on a day of misfortune﴾ [al-Qamar: 19]." He said: (p-18) "*Al-nahs* is calamity and hardship." He said: "Do the Arabs know that?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma say:

*It is all the same to him on whatever day he comes to it, whether it is an hour of misfortune he fears or an hour of greater fortune.*

Explaining *al-nahs* as calamity and hardship is an explanation by meaning, because ill omen is calamity and hardship. Zuhayr's contrasting of *al-nahs* with *al-as'ad* (the more fortunate) in his line makes this clear, and this is well known.

Some scholars claim that these days were at the end of Shawwal, and that the first of them was a Wednesday and the last of them was a Wednesday. There is no evidence for any of this.

What some scholars mention, that the day of continuous misfortune is the last Wednesday of the month, or simply any Wednesday, has led some who are attached to the pursuit of knowledge, and many of the common people, to regard the last Wednesday of every month as ill-omened. They refrain from undertaking travel, marriage, and similar matters on that day, thinking it to be a day of misfortune and ill omen, and that its misfortune is continuous upon all creatures at all times. This has no basis and no reliance may be placed upon it, and those who possess knowledge do not pay attention to it. This is because the misfortune of that day remained continuous only upon 'Ad alone, whom Allah destroyed on it, so that for them the punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state) and of the Hereafter was joined to the punishment of this world. Thus that ill omen became continuous upon them, a continuity with no cessation.

As for others than 'Ad, they are not held to account for the sin of 'Ad, because "no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" [al-An'am: 164].

Here we intend to mention some of the narrations by which those who believed in the continuance of misfortune on that day were deceived, so that we may show that they have no reliance.

The author of *al-Durr al-Manthur* said: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, regarding ﴿on a day of continuous misfortune﴾, that he said: "Wednesday."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: Judge by the oath together with a single witness. And he said: Wednesday is a day of continuous misfortune."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Ali, who said: "Jibril descended upon the Prophet (ﷺ) with (the ruling of) the oath together with a witness, and cupping, and Wednesday is a day of continuous misfortune."

(p-19) Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: 'The day of misfortune is Wednesday.'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the days, and he was asked about Wednesday. He said: 'It is a day of misfortune.' They said: 'How is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Allah drowned Pharaoh and his people on it, and destroyed 'Ad and Thamud.'"

Waki' in *al-Gharar*, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated with a weak chain from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The last Wednesday of the month is a day of continuous misfortune."

These narrations and others like them do not indicate the ill omen of Wednesday for one who has not disbelieved in Allah and has not disobeyed Him, because most of them are weak, and whatever of them is sound in meaning, its intended misfortune is its ill omen upon those disbelieving, disobedient people whom Allah destroyed on it because of their disbelief and their sins.

The conclusion is that ill omen and misfortune arise from and have their cause only in disbelief and sins.

As for one who is mindful of Allah and obedient to Him on that said Wednesday, there is no misfortune or ill omen for him in it. Whoever wishes to know misfortune, ill omen, wretchedness, calamity and hardship in their true sense, let him be certain that all of that lies in disobedience to Allah and in not complying with His command. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "We guided them" — the guidance meant here is the guidance of indication, clarification and direction, not the guidance of divine success (tawfiq) and selection (istifa').

The evidence for this is His saying after it: "but they preferred blindness over guidance," for if it were the guidance of tawfiq, its recipient would not have passed from guidance to blindness.

His saying in this noble verse: "but they preferred blindness over guidance" means: they chose disbelief over faith, gave it precedence over it, and exchanged it for it.

This meaning that we have mentioned is clarified by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾ [at-Tawbah: 23]. His saying in the verse of at-Tawbah, ﴿if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, agrees in meaning with His saying here: "they preferred blindness over guidance."

Similar in meaning is His saying: ﴿those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter and bar from the way of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 3].

So the word istahabba (to prefer) in the Qur'an is very often followed by 'ala (over), because it carries the meaning of ikhtara (to choose) and athara (to prefer).

We had already mentioned in surah Hud, in discussing His saying ﴿the likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf﴾, that blindness means disbelief, and that the blind in many verses means the disbeliever.

What this noble verse includes, that guidance comes in the Qur'an in its general meaning, which is clarification, indication and direction, does not preclude that guidance is sometimes used in the Qur'an in some places for the specific guidance, which is tawfiq and selection, as in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90].

Among the Qur'an's uses of guidance in its general meaning is His saying here: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾, i.e., We made clear to them the path of truth and commanded them to follow it, and the paths of evil and forbade them to follow them, through the tongue of our Prophet Salih — upon him and our Prophet be prayers and peace: ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾, i.e., they chose disbelief over faith after the truth had been made clear to them.

Among its uses in the general meaning is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ [al-Insan: 3], as shown by His following saying: ﴿either grateful or ungrateful﴾; for if it were the guidance of tawfiq, He would not have said "or ungrateful."

Among its uses in the specific meaning is His saying: ﴿so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90]; His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17]; and His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided﴾ [al-Kahf: 17].

By knowing these two usages, the resolution of a Qur'anic difficulty becomes easy. He affirmed guidance for our Prophet ﷺ in one verse, which is His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [ash-Shura: 52], and negated it for him in another verse, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas: 56].

It is known from what we have mentioned that the guidance affirmed for him ﷺ is the general guidance, which is clarification, indication and direction; and he ﷺ did this, clarifying the white path, such that its night is like its day, and none strays from it except one who is destined to perish.

The guidance negated for him in the verse ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas: 56] is the specific guidance, which is the bestowal of tawfiq by grace; because that is in the hand of Allah alone, and not in his hand ﷺ, as He said: ﴿And whoever Allah intends for his trial, you will not possess for him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whom Allah did not intend to purify their hearts﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Ma'idah: 41], and His saying: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who misguide﴾ [an-Nahl: 37]. Verses similar to this are many and well known.

Likewise His saying: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed, a guidance for mankind﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 185] — there is no contradiction in it between the generality of mankind in this verse and the particularity of the God-fearing in His saying: ﴿This is the Book, there is no doubt in it, a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2], because the general guidance for mankind is the general guidance, and the specific guidance for the God-fearing is the specific guidance, as is not hidden.

We have explained this in other than this place, and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾.

The fa' in His saying "so the thunderbolt seized them" is causal (sababiyyah), i.e., they preferred blindness over guidance, and because of that the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them.

Know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expressed the destruction by which He destroyed Thamud in various expressions. He mentioned it here by the name of the thunderbolt in His saying: ﴿so the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾, and His saying: ﴿So say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat: 13].

He also expressed it as a thunderbolt in surah adh-Dhariyat, in His saying: ﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them: Enjoy for a time.﴾ ﴿But they defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 43-44].

He expressed it as the Cry (al-sayhah) in verses of His Book:

• As His saying in surah Hud concerning His destruction of Thamud: ﴿And the Cry seized those who wronged, so they became in their homes prostrate﴾ ﴿as if they had never flourished there. Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ [Hud: 67-68].

• And His saying in al-Hijr: ﴿And they used to carve out of the mountains homes, secure﴾ ﴿So the Cry seized them at morning﴾ [al-Hijr: 82-83].

• And His saying in al-Qamar: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single Cry, and they became like the dry remnants of a fence-builder﴾ [al-Qamar: 31].

• And His saying in al-'Ankabut: ﴿And among them is one whom the Cry seized﴾, meaning by it Thamud mentioned in His saying before it: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings﴾, to the end of the verse [al-'Ankabut: 38].

He expressed it as the quake (al-rajfah) in surah al-A'raf, in His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, and said: O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers﴾ ﴿So the quake seized them﴾, to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 77-78].

He expressed it as destruction (al-tadmir) in surah an-Naml, in His saying: ﴿So look how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people, all together﴾ [an-Naml: 51].

He expressed it as al-taghiyah (the overwhelming) in al-Haqqah, in His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming﴾ [al-Haqqah: 5].

He expressed it as al-damdamah (the crushing) in ash-Shams, in His saying: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ ﴿so their Lord crushed them over their sin and leveled it﴾ [ash-Shams: 14].

He expressed it as punishment (al-'adhab) in surah ash-Shu'ara', in His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung her, and they became regretful﴾ ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 157-158].

The meaning of all these expressions returns to one thing, which is that Allah sent upon them a Cry that destroyed them, and the Cry is the terrifying, destructive sound.

The word sa'iqah is also used for the terrifying, destructive sound, and for the burning fire, and for both together. Because of the great magnitude and terror of the Cry, from above them, the earth quaked beneath them, i.e., it moved with a strong motion; so there were gathered in it that it was a Cry, a thunderbolt, and a quake, and that this was destruction is clear. It was called "overwhelming" (taghiyah) because it is an event that exceeds the limit in its force and severity of destruction.

Al-tughyan in the language of the Arabs is exceeding the limit, and from it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Haqqah: 11], i.e., it exceeded the bounds which water ordinarily reaches.

Know that the verified view is that what is meant by al-taghiyah in His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming﴾ [al-Haqqah: 5] is the Cry by which Allah destroyed them, as His following saying clarifies: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6].

This is contrary to those who claimed that al-taghiyah is a verbal noun like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah, and that the meaning is that they were destroyed by their transgression, i.e., by their disbelief and their denial of their prophet, as in His saying: ﴿Thamud denied by its transgression﴾ [ash-Shams: 11].

And contrary to those who claimed that al-taghiyah is their most wretched one who rose up and hamstrung the she-camel, and that they were destroyed because of his act, which is his hamstringing of the she-camel; all of this is contrary to the verified view.

The correct view, God willing, is what we have mentioned; the context indicates it, and more than one scholar has chosen it.

As for His saying: ﴿So their Lord crushed them over their sin﴾ [ash-Shams: 14], it does not contradict what we have mentioned; because the meaning of "damdama 'alayhim rabbuhum bi-dhanbihim" is that He made the punishment fall upon them and clothed them in it, because of their sin.

Az-Zamakhshari said regarding the meaning of damdama: it is from the repetition of their saying: "a she-camel madmumah," when it is clothed with fat.

As for the application of 'adhab to it in surah ash-Shu'ara', it is clear, and thus the return of the meaning of the mentioned verses to one thing becomes evident.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment" is an attribution by verbal noun (al-na't bi-al-masdar), because al-hun is a verbal noun meaning humiliation (al-hawan), and describing by a verbal noun is a well-known Arabic usage, to which he pointed in the Khulasah with his saying:

"They described with the verbal noun often, so they kept it singular and masculine."

It is construed in one of two ways: First, that it is by omission of a modified noun, i.e., "the punishment of the one possessing humiliation."

Second, that it is by way of intensification, as if the punishment, because of its intense attribution of the humiliation that attaches to the one upon whom it falls, has become as if it were the very humiliation itself, as is known in its proper place.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾ serves as an emphasis in meaning to His saying: "they preferred blindness over guidance," because each of them is a cause for the thunderbolt seizing them. So the fa' in His saying "so they were seized" is causal, and the ba' in His saying "bima kanu" (because of what they were) is causal. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 41, verse 25:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We appointed for them companions, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾.

The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) have various expressions regarding the meaning of His words "We appointed" (qayyadna), and some of these expressions return, in meaning, to others.

Like the saying of some of them: ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾, meaning: We brought them to them and brought them together for them.

And like the saying of some of them: "qayyadna" means "hayya'na" (We prepared).

And the saying of some of them: "qayyadna" means "sallatna" (We gave power over).

And the saying of some of them: meaning "ba'athna" (We sent) and "wakkalna" (We entrusted).

And the saying of some of them: "qayyadna" means "sabbabna" (We caused).

And the saying of some of them: "qadarna" (We decreed). And other expressions of this kind. All of these expressions return to one thing, which is that Allah, blessed and exalted, prepared for the disbelievers companions from the devils who lead them astray from guidance, make disbelief and sins appear attractive to them, and decreed them over them.

"Al-qurana'" (companions) is the plural of "qarin" (companion), and they are, in truth, their companions from among the devils.

As for His saying ﴿who made attractive to them what was before them﴾, meaning: of the matters of this world, to the point that they preferred it over the Hereafter (p-27) ﴿and what was behind them﴾, meaning: of the matters of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the resurrection.

What this noble verse includes is that He, exalted, appointed for the disbelievers companions from the devils who lead them astray from guidance. He made this clear in other places of His Book.

In some of them He added the reason for their being appointed to them, and that, along with leading them astray, they think they are rightly guided; and that the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection wishes that between him and his companion from the devils there were a great distance, and that companion blames him that Day. As He, exalted, said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾. ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think that they are guided﴾. ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 36-38].

His placing of His saying "We appoint for him a devil" after His saying "whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful" is the placing of the consequence after the condition, which indicates that the cause of his being appointed a devil is his heedlessness of the remembrance of the Most Merciful.

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws﴾ [an-Nas: 4], because "al-waswas" (the whisperer) is one who whispers much in order to lead people astray by it, and "al-khannas" (the one who withdraws) is one who often withdraws and returns from misleading people. It derives from their saying "khanasa" (with fatha) "yakhnusu" (with damma), meaning he withdrew.

So he is a whisperer when one is heedless of the remembrance of the Most Merciful, and a withdrawer when the remembrance of the Most Merciful is made. This is what the aforementioned verse of az-Zukhruf indicates, and what His saying also indicates: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾. ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [an-Nahl: 99-100]. This is because those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him are heedless of the remembrance of the Most Merciful, and because of that Allah appointed him for them, and he led them astray.

Among the verses that indicate that the devils are appointed to the disbelievers in order to lead them astray is His saying: ﴿Have We not sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with strong incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83]. We have clarified the verses indicating this in the surah of Maryam, in our discussion of His saying: ﴿Have We not sent the devils upon the disbelievers﴾, and we explained there the statements of the people of knowledge regarding the meaning of ﴿inciting them with strong incitement﴾.

We have also explained there that among the verses indicating this is His saying: ﴿And the day He gathers them all together: "O assembly of jinn, you have taken much of mankind"﴾ [al-An'am: 128], meaning: you have taken much of mankind for misleading them in the life of this world. And His saying: ﴿And their brothers (the devils) extend them in error, then they do not hold back﴾ [al-A'raf: 202].

(p-28) Also among them is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And he had already led astray from among you a great multitude﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60-62], and other verses besides these.

His saying in the verse of az-Zukhruf: ﴿Wretched is the companion﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 38] indicates that the devil companions mentioned in the verse of Fussilat and the verse of az-Zukhruf, and others, deserve severe blame. He, exalted, has stated this clearly in the surah of an-Nisa', in His saying: ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is he as a companion﴾ [an-Nisa': 38]. This is because His saying "fa-sa'a qarinan" (then evil is he as a companion) has the same meaning as "fa-bi'sa al-qarin" (wretched is the companion), since each of "sa'a" and "bi'sa" is a rigid verb used to express blame, as he mentioned in the Khulasah (of Ibn Malik) in his saying:

"Make 'ka-bi'sa' and 'sa'a' [verbs of blame], and make a verb from the triliteral form 'ka-ni'ma' (a verb of praise) [in the same way]."

Know that Allah, exalted, has made clear that the disbelievers whom their devil companions have led astray think that they are upon guidance. They consider the worst of misguidance to be the best of guidance, as He, exalted, said about them: ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think that they are guided﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 37]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided﴾ [7].

He, exalted, also made clear that because of that false assumption they are the greatest losers in deeds, in His saying: ﴿Say: "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think that they are doing good work"﴾ [al-Kahf: 103-104].

As for His saying in the verse of az-Zukhruf: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 36], it comes from their saying "'asha" (with fatha) "'an ash-shay'" "ya'sha" (with damma), meaning his sight weakened in perceiving it. Allah's words: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾.

What He, may He be exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that He is not unjust to His slaves, He mentioned in other places:

• As in His words in Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forth, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾ ﴿[Those] who say, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 182].

• And His words in al-Anfal: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forth, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾ ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾ [al-Anfal: 51-52].

• And His words in al-Hajj: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forth, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah﴾ and the verse [al-Hajj: 10-11].

• And His words in Surat Qaf: ﴿The word is not changed with Me, and I am not ever unjust to the slaves﴾ [Qaf: 29].

In these verses there is a well-known question: the word (ظَلّام, zallam) in them is an intensive form (صيغة مبالغة, sigha mubalagha: a form expressing intensity or frequency), and it is known that negating the intensive form does not necessarily entail negating the act itself at its root.

So your saying, for example: "Zayd is not a great killer of men" negates only his excessiveness in killing them, and does not contradict that he may have killed some men.

And it is known that the intended meaning of negating the intensiveness in the mentioned verses is negating injustice at its root.

The answer to this problem is in four aspects. The first: many verses have shown that the intended meaning of the negation of the intensive form in the mentioned verses is the negation of injustice at its root.

When separate evidences indicate that the negation of an intensive form is meant to negate the act itself at its root, there is no problem, because the evidence establishes the intended meaning.

The verses indicating this are many and well known, such as:

• His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [al-Nisa': 40].

• His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus: 44].

• His words: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

• His words: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya': 47].

As well as other verses, as we have already explained in Surat al-Kahf and al-Anbiya'.

The second aspect: Allah, may He be exalted, negated His injustice to the slaves, and the slaves are extremely numerous. The injustice negated of them entails that its quantity would be as great as their number. So it suits that the intensive form is used, to indicate the greatness of what is negated, which follows the greatness of the number of slaves from whom injustice is negated. For if injustice fell upon every slave, even a little, the sum of that injustice would be extremely great, as you see.

By this you know the direction of the expression with the intensive form: that what is meant is the negation of the very root of injustice from each one of those slaves, who are extremely numerous, far exalted is He above wronging anyone at all, as the mentioned Qur'anic verses have shown. And in the hadith: "O My slaves, I have forbidden injustice for Myself," the hadith.

The third aspect: what justifies the intensive form is that His punishment, may He be exalted, is so great and severe that, were it not that those punished deserve that punishment because of their disbelief and sins, He would be an extremely great wrongdoer, of greatly aggravated injustice, far exalted is He above that with great exaltedness.

This aspect and the one before it were indicated by al-Zamakhshari in Surat al-Anfal.

The fourth aspect: what some scholars of Arabic and some exegetes have mentioned, that the intended negation in His words: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾ is the negation of attributing injustice to Him. This is because the form fa''al (فَعّال) is used with the meaning of attribution (نِسْبَة, nisba), so it dispenses with the ya' of attribution (ياء النسب, ya' al-nasab), as indicated in the Khulasa (the summary of Ibn Malik's Alfiyya) by his saying:

"And with fa'il and fa''al, fa'il in attribution, it suffices from the ya', so accept it."

The meaning of the mentioned line is that the three forms mentioned in it, which are fa'il like ẓālim (one who wrongs), fa''al like ẓallām, and fa'il like faraḥ, each of them may be used with the meaning of attribution, so the ya' of attribution is dispensed with by them. An example of fa'il is the saying of al-Hutay'a in his satire of al-Zibriqan ibn Badr al-Tamimi:

"Leave generosity, do not travel in pursuit of it; sit, for you are the one who has food and clothing."

So the meaning of "al-ṭā'im al-kāsī" (the one with food and clothing) is the attribution, i.e., one who possesses food and clothing. And another's saying, which is one of Sibawayh's evidences:

"You deceived me and claimed that you are a possessor of milk in summer, dealing in dates."

That is, one who possesses milk and dates. And the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

"Leave me with them, O Umayma, a tired one, and a night I endure, slow in its stars."

So his saying "nāṣib" means one who has fatigue (naṣab). An example of fa''al is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"He is not one with a spear to stab me with it, nor one with a sword, nor one with a bow-maker (nabbāl)."

So his saying "wa laysa bi-nabbāl" means: he is not one who possesses arrows (nabl). What indicates it is his saying before it: "nor one with a spear," "nor one with a sword."

Al-Ushmuni said, after citing the mentioned line: The author (i.e., Ibn Malik) said: "On this basis the verifiers interpreted the words of Allah, ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the slaves﴾, i.e., not one possessing injustice." End of quote.

What he attributed to Ibn Malik has been affirmed by more than one of the grammarians and exegetes. An example in fa'il (فَعِل) is the saying of the rajaz poet, which is one of Sibawayh's evidences:

"He is not a night-person, but a day-person; I do not travel by night, but I set out in the early morning."

So his saying "nahir" means "nahāri" (of the day). We have already explained the meaning of injustice with its Arabic evidences in several places in this blessed book. And Allah knows best.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾.

The discussion of its like has already passed in *Surat al-A'raf* (the Surah of the Heights), in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 187]. And in *Surat al-An'am* (the Surah of the Cattle), at His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And no female carries or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾.

We have already discussed it in *Surat al-Ra'd* (the Surah of Thunder), in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8], and what follows.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will be certain that there is for them no escape.﴾

Al-zann (assumption, supposition) here carries the meaning of al-yaqin (certainty), because the disbelievers, on the Day of Resurrection, when they witness the punishment and see the realities, know at that time that there is for them no escape (mahis), i.e., there is for them no refuge and no shelter.

It is apparent that al-mahis is a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi), from haasa yahis, meaning to swerve, deviate, or flee.

What we have mentioned, that al-zann in this noble verse means al-yaqin and al-ilm (knowledge), is the verification (al-tahqiq), God willing, because on the Day of Resurrection the realities will be unveiled, so the disbelievers will attain knowledge of them, with no doubt troubling them in that regard, as He, exalted is He, said of them that they will say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to earth]; we will act righteously. Indeed, we are now certain.﴾ [As-Sajdah: 12]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿How [clearly] they will hear and see the Day they come to Us!﴾ [Maryam: 38]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We have removed from you your covering, and your sight this day is sharp.﴾ [Qaf: 22]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you could but see when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord."﴾ [Al-An'am: 30]. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in surah "An-Naml," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter.﴾ [An-Naml: 66].

It is known that al-zann is used in the Arabic language, in which the Qur'an was revealed, with two meanings. The first: doubt, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, assumption does not avail against the truth at all.﴾ [An-Najm: 28], and His saying, exalted is He, about the disbelievers: ﴿We think not but an assumption, and we are not convinced.﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 32].

The second: the use of al-zann to mean knowledge and certainty. From it is His saying here: ﴿And they will be certain that there is for them no escape.﴾ [Fussilat: 48], i.e., they will be certain that for them on the Day of Resurrection there is no escape, i.e., no flight and no fleeing from the punishment of their Lord. In this same meaning is His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 53], i.e., they were certain of that and knew it. And His saying: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 46]. And His saying: ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 249]. And His saying: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account."﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 19-20]. So al-zann in all the verses mentioned is in the sense of al-yaqin.

A parallel to this in the speech of the Arabs is the verse of Duraid ibn al-Simmah:

"So I said to them: 'Be certain of two thousand armored men, their chiefs in the Persian mail, well-woven.'"

And the verse of Umayrah ibn Tariq:

"That you raid my people, and I sit among you, and I make of my assumption an unseen, stoned [target]."

In the two verses mentioned, al-zann means al-yaqin. The mental verb in the verse mentioned, which is His saying: ﴿And they will be certain that there is for them no escape﴾, is suspended (mu'allaq) from governing the two objects because of the negation by the particle (ma) in His saying: ﴿that there is for them no escape﴾, as he indicated in the Khulasah with his saying:

"And adopt suspension before the negation 'ma'."

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 50:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine (due to me), and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best (reward)."﴾

(p. 36) We have already mentioned the verses that clarify it in Surah "Al-Kahf," in discussing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this, and some of the sound hadiths that agree with them, in the surah of Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him.﴾ [Yunus: 12].

The Exalted said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ — the verse.

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah "al-Mu'min" (Ghafir), in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ — the verse [Ghafir: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 54:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Verily, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord.﴾

Al-Mirya (doubt, suspicion) means al-shakk (doubt). What this noble verse includes of the disbelievers' doubt concerning the resurrection (al-ba'th) and the recompense (al-jaza'), we have already presented the verses that clarify it, and what follows from it of abiding forever in the Fire, in surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, but they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire﴾ [al-Furqan: 11].
